issues.t: Shift lever can move out of Park (recall)
issues.sym: On automatic cars, the shifter can be moved out of Park without pressing the brake or the shifter button, even with the key out. The car can roll away on a slope.
issues.why: A defect in the automatic shifter assembly let it leave Park too easily. Suzuki recall 98V225002; GM ran the same campaign on the twin Metro.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake when you park. Check the VIN for open recalls with NHTSA or a Suzuki-trained shop; the shifter replacement was free.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint can separate
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, loose or wandering steering, uneven tire wear. In the worst case a front wheel collapses inward.
issues.why: The lower ball joints wear and can pull out of the control arm, especially on rusty cars. Suzuki sent US dealers a bulletin stressing inspection and upkeep of these ball joints.
issues.next: Have the ball joints checked at every inspection or tire rotation, and replace any that are loose before driving further.

issues.sym: Clunks or creaks from underneath, rust flakes, or a car that tracks badly after hitting a bump.
issues.why: Road salt eats into the suspension and its mounting points on these older cars. Suzuki sent dealers a reminder to inspect suspension parts for rust damage.
issues.next: If you live where roads are salted, have the suspension, subframe and brake lines checked on a lift once a year.

issues.sym: The engine dies at low speed or even on the highway, then restarts. It can happen again right after a repair.
issues.why: A 2001 owner reported repeated stalling that the dealer could not find. Metro owners report the same thing; sensor, idle control, ignition and fuel delivery faults are common causes. The 1996-2001 Swift shares its body and 1.3L engine with the Geo and Chevrolet Metro.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Write down when it happens to help the shop find the cause.

issues.sym: A knock or rattle at the front of the engine, loss of power, then the engine shuts off.
issues.why: Metro owners report the bolt that holds the crankshaft pulley rusting and breaking. A loose pulley can damage the timing belt. The 1996-2001 Swift shares its body and 1.3L engine with the Geo and Chevrolet Metro.
issues.next: If you hear a new knock at the front of the engine, stop and have it checked before the timing belt is damaged.

issues.t: Airbag deploys without a real crash
issues.sym: The front airbag goes off after hitting a dip or swerving, with little or no impact.
issues.why: Owners of 1998 and 2000 Swifts reported airbags deploying unexpectedly, including one that injured the driver and passenger.
issues.next: If your airbag light is on or an airbag went off without a crash, report it to NHTSA and have the airbag system inspected by a qualified shop.

issues.t: Front seat backs fold back in a rear crash
issues.sym: After being hit from behind, the front seat backs bend or collapse backward.
issues.why: An owner of a 2000 Swift reported both front seats folding back in a rear-end crash, injuring the people in them.
issues.next: After any rear impact, have the seat frames and recliners checked before using the car again.

issues.sym: The rear hatch pops open on the road.
issues.why: A 2001 owner reported the hatch latch letting go at about 45 mph.
issues.next: If the hatch ever opens by itself, stop and secure it. Have the latch and striker checked or replaced, and don't carry anyone or anything loose in the back until it's fixed.

issues.t: Front brakes grab and pull hard to one side
issues.sym: When you brake, the front brakes lock and the car pulls sharply left or right.
issues.why: A 2001 owner reported the front brakes locking at about 55 mph. A sticking caliper, a contaminated pad or a collapsed brake hose can make one side grab.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected before driving at speed again.

issues.sym: The engine turns over normally but won't fire.
issues.why: Metro owners report cranking with no start at high mileage, even after checking timing, spark and fuel. A failing distributor pickup, ignition module or fuel pump relay is often to blame. The 1996-2001 Swift shares its body and 1.3L engine with the Geo and Chevrolet Metro.
issues.next: Have a shop test for spark and fuel pressure while the problem is happening.

issues.sym: Clicking when turning, or a clunk or vibration when you accelerate.
issues.why: Front axle failures are among the top Metro complaints, often around 95,000 miles. A torn rubber boot lets dirt in and wears out the joint. The 1996-2001 Swift shares its body and 1.3L engine with the Geo and Chevrolet Metro.
issues.next: Check the axle boots for tears or grease. Replace a clicking axle before it breaks.

issues.sym: A bouncy or floaty ride at highway speed, extra body roll, or clunks over bumps.
issues.why: Worn front struts are the most common Metro problem on RepairPal, often around 75,000 miles. The 1996-2001 Swift shares its body and 1.3L engine with the Geo and Chevrolet Metro.
issues.next: Have the struts checked. Replace them in pairs and get an alignment.

issues.t: Check engine light from loose or worn gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: A gas cap that doesn't seal sets an evaporative emissions code. The 1996-2001 Swift shares its body and 1.3L engine with the Geo and Chevrolet Metro.
issues.next: Tighten or replace the gas cap and see if the light clears after a few days of driving. If not, have the code read.

issues.t: Brake pedal pulsates from warped rotors
issues.sym: The brake pedal pulses or the steering wheel shakes when you brake.
issues.why: The front rotors run out of true, often because the wheel nuts were tightened unevenly.
issues.next: Have the rotors resurfaced or replaced, and make sure the shop tightens the wheel nuts with a torque wrench.

issues.sym: The interior light stays on with the doors closed, and the battery can go flat overnight.
issues.why: A worn door jamb switch keeps telling the car a door is open.
issues.next: Find which door switch is bad and replace it. It's a simple part.

issues.t: Owner's manual missing child seat anchor instructions (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can see on the car. The owner's manual lacks instructions for the child seat anchors.
issues.why: The 2000 manual left out the child restraint anchorage instructions required by federal rules, so a child seat might be attached wrong. Suzuki recall 00V286000 sent owners a new manual.
issues.next: Follow your child seat's own instructions and have a certified car seat technician check the installation.
issues.sevReason: Owner manual missing instructions; not a hardware failure.
